api-reference/overview.title: API Overview
api-reference/overview.description: Vectora exposes a REST API at /v1/ for programmatic access to all AI and workspace features.

api-reference/webhooks.title: Webhooks
api-reference/webhooks.description: Vectora can send HTTP POST requests to your endpoints when certain events occur.

getting-started/first-workspace.title: First Workspace
getting-started/first-workspace.description: A Vectora workspace contains users, projects, and a shared knowledge base. This guide walks through the initial configuration after installation.

getting-started/installation.title: Installation
getting-started/installation.description: Vectora ships as a single Docker image. All you need is a Linux server with Docker installed.

getting-started/introduction.title: What is Vectora?
getting-started/introduction.description: Vectora is a self-hosted AI agent platform with multi-user web chat, RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), MCP integrations, and a REST API. Your data never leaves your server.

getting-started/quick-start.title: Quick Start
getting-started/quick-start.description: Get from zero to your first AI conversation in under 5 minutes.

getting-started/upgrade-from-cli.title: Upgrade from CLI
getting-started/upgrade-from-cli.description: Vectora ships updates via its built-in auto-update mechanism. You can also upgrade manually if auto-update is disabled.

getting-started/vectora-token.title: VECTORA_TOKEN
getting-started/vectora-token.description: The VECTORA_TOKEN is the secret that authenticates your Vectora instance with your license. Without a valid token, Vectora runs in restricted mode (no AI responses, no RAG).

guides/api-keys.title: API Keys
guides/api-keys.description: API keys allow external services to interact with Vectora programmatically.

guides/data-migration.title: Data Migration
guides/data-migration.description: This guide covers migrating data into Vectora: bulk document import, moving between Vectora instances, and exporting data.

guides/git-workflows.title: Git Workflows
guides/git-workflows.description: Vectora's Coder Agent has built-in Git awareness. It can read history, create branches, commit, and open PRs — all from a chat message.

guides/github-actions.title: GitHub Actions
guides/github-actions.description: Automate Vectora tasks in your CI/CD pipeline using the official GitHub Action or the TypeScript SDK.

guides/ide-integration.title: IDE Integration
guides/ide-integration.description: Vectora integrates with VS Code and JetBrains IDEs, letting you chat with the agent directly from your editor.

guides/mcp-integration.title: MCP Integration
guides/mcp-integration.description: Vectora exposes an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets any MCP-compatible client — Claude Desktop, VS Code, Cursor, and others — use Vectora as a context source and agent tool.

guides/n8n-workflows.title: n8n Workflows
guides/n8n-workflows.description: Connect Vectora to n8n to build no-code automations: Slack → agent → Notion, webhook → RAG query → email reply, and more.

guides/rag-guide.title: RAG Pipeline
guides/rag-guide.description: Vectora uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to let the AI answer questions about your documents with high precision.

guides/sdk-python.title: Python SDK
guides/sdk-python.description: The vectora Python package provides a type-safe client for the Vectora REST API.

guides/sdk-typescript.title: TypeScript SDK
guides/sdk-typescript.description: The @vectora/sdk package provides a fully typed client for the Vectora REST API, compatible with Node.js, Bun, and browser environments.

guides/vps-deploy.title: Deploy on a VPS
guides/vps-deploy.description: This guide walks through deploying Vectora on a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 VPS. The same steps apply to any Linux server (Debian 12+, Rocky Linux 9+).

guides/webhooks.title: Webhooks
guides/webhooks.description: Vectora (Pro plan) can send HTTP POST requests to your endpoints when specific events occur.

intro.title: Introduction
intro.description: Vectora is a self-hosted AI agent with RAG, MCP and multi-user web chat. Your data never leaves your server.

reference/acp-server.title: ACP Server
reference/acp-server.description: Vectora implements the Agent Communication Protocol (ACP), allowing it to act as a sub-agent in multi-agent systems.

reference/agents.title: Agents Reference
reference/agents.description: Vectora uses a multi-agent architecture built on LangGraph. The orchestrator routes tasks to specialized agents based on intent detection. Each agent has a defined toolset and a specific role in the execution graph.

reference/cli.title: CLI Reference
reference/cli.description: The vectora CLI is the primary way to manage your Vectora installation.

reference/config.title: Configuration Reference
reference/config.description: Vectora is configured via a .env file in the same directory as your docker-compose.yml.

reference/mcp-server.title: MCP Server
reference/mcp-server.description: Vectora exposes an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, making it usable as a tool source for any MCP-compatible AI client (Claude Desktop, Zed, Cursor, custom agents).

reference/storage-backends.title: Storage Backends
reference/storage-backends.description: Vectora stores uploaded files (documents, exports) in a configurable backend.

reference/tools.title: Built-in Tools
reference/tools.description: Vectora agents have access to a set of built-in tools that let them interact with the filesystem, terminal, web, and your knowledge bases. Tools are invoked automatically by the orchestrator based on the task.

self-hosting/backup-restore.title: Backup & Restore
self-hosting/backup-restore.description: Vectora's persistent state lives in two places:

self-hosting/kubernetes.title: Kubernetes
self-hosting/kubernetes.description: This guide covers deploying Vectora on Kubernetes using Helm or raw manifests.

self-hosting/monitoring.title: Monitoring
self-hosting/monitoring.description: Vectora exposes Prometheus metrics, structured JSON logs, and a /health endpoint.

self-hosting/nginx-traefik.title: Nginx / Traefik
self-hosting/nginx-traefik.description: Vectora runs on port 8080. Use Nginx as a reverse proxy with Let's Encrypt for HTTPS.

self-hosting/storage-backends.title: Storage Backends
self-hosting/storage-backends.description: See Reference → Storage Backends for a full reference on all storage options.

self-hosting/updates.title: Updating Vectora
self-hosting/updates.description: Vectora uses semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Patch releases are always safe to apply; minor and major releases include migration notes.
